title: What does rmdir do?
prompt:
Jonas keeps a cheat sheet of commands. Save the one-line description of `rmdir` from its manual page, the line that starts with `rmdir (1)`, into a file `rmdir.txt` in Mira’s home directory.

Don’t copy it by hand: let a command print it and redirect that into the file.
hints: Every man page starts with a NAME section: the command and a one-line description. Some commands print just that line.
`whatis` and `man -f` print the NAME line of a manual page.
Redirect the output into the file with `> rmdir.txt`.
check:
if [ ! -e rmdir.txt ]; then no "There is no rmdir.txt yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "rmdir.txt exists."
if grep -q '^rmdir (1) *- remove empty directories' rmdir.txt; then ok "It holds the NAME line of rmdir’s man page."
else no "It doesn’t hold the line “rmdir (1) - remove empty directories” as whatis or man -f print it."; fi

title: The usage line of mkdir
prompt:
Most GNU tools print a short help text with `--help`. Its first line is the usage line, which shows how to call the tool.

Save only the first line of the help text of `mkdir` into `usage.txt` in Mira’s home directory.
hints: Try `mkdir --help` first and look at its first line.
`head -n 1` keeps only the first line of whatever it reads.
Join the two with a pipe, `|`, and redirect the result with `> usage.txt`.
check:
if [ ! -e usage.txt ]; then no "There is no usage.txt yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "usage.txt exists."
want=$(mkdir --help | head -n 1)
if [ "$(cat usage.txt)" = "$want" ]; then ok "It holds exactly the usage line: $want"
elif grep -qF "$want" usage.txt; then no "It holds the usage line, but other lines too. Keep only the first line."
else no "It doesn’t hold the first line of mkdir --help."; fi
